No, that is not true. Romansh is one of the four official languages of Switzerland (alongside German, French, and Italian) but it is only an official language in the specific linguistic regions where it is spoken, primarily in the canton of Graubünden.

For federal authorities:
- Romansh is an official language for communication with Romansh-speaking citizens.
- Citizens have the right to address federal authorities in Romansh and receive a response in Romansh.
- However, federal legislation, official publications, and most federal documents are not produced in Romansh; they are primarily in German, French, and Italian.

So while Romansh has official status and recognition, it is not applicable to all official documents for all federal authorities across the entire country.
